title: Birmingham Terminal Station
geometryBasis: The named station outline and shed on 1911 Sanborn sheet 21 establish each building mass. The trace is registered to the surviving Fifth Avenue North tunnel and Carraway corridor. The architect gives overall site and canopy dimensions.
sectionBasis: Marye’s 1909 American Architect report and plates establish the 130-ft towers, 100-ft dome, buff-to-terracotta brick, terracotta roofs, grey sandstone, bronze frames, subway geometry, and reinforced concrete umbrella sheds. Qualla’s exact 1909–10 and 1913 exterior postcards establish facade details and massing.
limitations: The former passenger station and attached train shed are shown circa 1913. The demolition date bounds historical visibility. The full interior, freestanding powerhouse, streetcar track, distant railroad yard and later Magic City sign are outside this scope.

Architect’s drawings, dimensions, early exterior postcards and the 1911 survey govern the model. Decorative relief, actual finish tint, baggage and express wing roof breaks, rails and portions of the rear platform envelope are interpreted.

The present-day original terrain is preserved as an independent reference. Historic floor elevations and the grade of the subway approach are approximate. A narrow modeled road cut reveals the original west portal in geographic views.
